text.en:
Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 6th November 2009 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2009” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock of the coin.
The Northern Wetlands of Singapore consists of Kranji and Lim Chu Kang, while the Central Catchment encompasses the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.
Through the careful preservation of biodiversity and sensitive addition of new trails and boardwalks, more people have been able to appreciate and enjoy the ecological beauty of these 2 areas.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2009” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin.
• Kranji & Lim Chu Kang
This is located at the northwest corner of Singapore, away from the hustle and bustle of the city. This area is anchored by the 130-hectare Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve and the tranquil Kranji Reservoir. The main feature of this coin is the Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve, an idyllic nature reserve where visitors can observe migratory birds and view the vast species of native mangrove flora without getting their feet wet. Depicted on the right is the 18-metre tall Bird Observatory Tower that offers panoramic views of the Reserve and the surrounding areas. At the left bottom are the distinct tidal gates of Kranji Reservoir used to regulate the level of water in the reservoir. The coin also features some common animals found in the area to capture its fauna. The denomination is at the top centre of the coin.
• Central Catchment
This is a stone’s throw away from the city and home to an expanse of tropical rainforest and 4 reservoirs – MacRitchie, Upper and Lower Pierce and Upper Seletar.
The coin highlights the MacRitchie Reservoir Park and the Upper Seletar Reservoir Park. Harmonising with the design of the Kranji and Lim Chu Kang coin, the iconic observatory tower at Upper Seletar Reservoir Park is featured on the right while at the bottom, there is the 250-metre long HSBC TreeTop Walk, a suspension bridge in MacRitchie Reservoir Park that offers a canopy view of the lush forest below. At the centre is MacRitchie Reservoir’s most recognisable feature – the floating pavilion popular with families and friends for a quiet respite. Some sports activities commonly held at MacRitchie have also been incorporated. The denomination is at the lower left of the coin.
(a) Reverse Design of the $1 Silver Proof Coin (Kranji & Lim Chu Kang).

(c) Common Obverse Design for the $1 Silver Proof Coins (Kranji & Lim Chu Kang and Central Catchment).
(d) Reverse Design of the $1 Cupro-Nickel Proof-Like Coin (Kranji & Lim Chu Kang).
(e) Reverse Design of the $1 Cupro-Nickel Proof-Like Coin (Central Catchment).
(f) Common Obverse Design for the $1 Cupro-Nickel Proof-Like Coins (Kranji & Lim Chu Kang and Central Catchment).
